:::{#thm-continuity-probability}
#### Continuity of probability

If $A_1 \supseteq A_2 \supseteq \cdots$ are events
with $\bigcap_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i = \emptyset$,
then:

$$\lim_{n \to \infty} \Pr(A_n) = 0$$

:::

::: proof

For each $i$, let $B_i \eqdef A_i \setminus A_{i+1}$,
the outcomes in $A_i$ but not in $A_{i+1}$.
Each $B_i = A_i \cap (\samplespace \setminus A_{i+1})$ is an event,
by [closure properties of a $\sigma$-algebra](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/measures.html#thm-sigma-algebra-closure).

*The $B_i$ are pairwise disjoint.*
For $i < j$,
$B_j \subseteq A_j \subseteq A_{i+1}$,
while $B_i$ has no outcomes in $A_{i+1}$,
so $B_i \cap B_j = \emptyset$.

*$A_n = \bigcup_{i=n}^{\infty} B_i$ for each $n$.*
For $i \ge n$, $B_i \subseteq A_i \subseteq A_n$,
so the union is contained in $A_n$.
Conversely, let $\outcome \in A_n$.
Since $\bigcap_{i} A_i = \emptyset$,
$\outcome$ is not in every $A_i$;
since the $A_i$ are nested,
the indices $i$ with $\outcome \in A_i$ are $1, \ldots, m$ for some $m \ge n$.
Then $\outcome \in A_m$ and $\outcome \notin A_{m+1}$,
so $\outcome \in B_m$.

*$\Pr(A_1)$ is finite.*
The events $A_1$ and $\samplespace \setminus A_1$ are disjoint with union $\samplespace$,
so @cor-probability-finitely-additive applies to them:

$$
\ba
\Pr(A_1)
&\le \Pr(A_1) + \Pr(\samplespace \setminus A_1)
&& \text{(} \Pr(\samplespace \setminus A_1) \ge 0 \text{)} \\
&= \Pr(\samplespace)
&& \text{(finite additivity of } \Pr \text{)} \\
&= 1
&& \text{(definition of a probability measure)}
\ea
$$

*The limit.*
For each $n$:

$$
\ba
\Pr(A_n)
&= \Prf{\bigcup_{i=n}^{\infty} B_i}
&& \text{(} A_n = \bigcup_{i=n}^{\infty} B_i \text{)} \\
&= \sum_{i=n}^{\infty} \Pr(B_i)
&& \text{(countable additivity; the } B_i \text{ are pairwise disjoint)}
\ea
$$

With $n = 1$, this says the series $\sumto{i}{\infty} \Pr(B_i)$
has the finite total $\Pr(A_1)$.
So, for $n \ge 2$:

$$
\ba
\Pr(A_n)
&= \sumto{i}{\infty} \Pr(B_i) - \sumto{i}{n-1} \Pr(B_i)
&& \text{(split off the first } n - 1 \text{ terms; the total is finite)} \\
&= \Pr(A_1) - \sumto{i}{n-1} \Pr(B_i)
&& \text{(the case } n = 1 \text{)}
\ea
$$

As $n \to \infty$,
the partial sums $\sumto{i}{n-1} \Pr(B_i)$ converge to the total $\Pr(A_1)$,
so $\Pr(A_n) \to \Pr(A_1) - \Pr(A_1) = 0$.

:::
